plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: Bulbous perennials with large trumpet-shaped flowers atop thick, hollow stalks. In the Southern Hemisphere they bloom outdoors in midsummer gardens, and in the Northern Hemisphere they are forced indoors as popular winter holiday plants.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late December to March (outdoors in the Southern Hemisphere); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Native to South America; cultivated worldwide, outdoors in Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand and indoors in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Amaryllis flower stalks can grow up to an inch per day under warm conditions, and the bulbs can rebloom for decades with proper care.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that open in the cool season. It thrives in mild, humid climates and brightens winter gardens when little else is blooming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (peaking December to March)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely grown in the southeastern United States, the Pacific Northwest, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and thousands of cultivars have been bred over centuries in Japan and beyond.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with feathery fern-like leaves that produces spectacular clusters of large flowers. It blooms in tropical and subtropical regions, with strong displays in the Southern Hemisphere summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly November to February; at other times in the Northern tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, Brazil, India, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Although it is one of the world's most celebrated ornamental trees, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers with golden stamens. It blooms in the cold of winter, often pushing flowers up through frost and light snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a true rose but belongs to the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.
